items.title: One main recipe
paragraphs: A stoichiometric mixture of 0.481 g (15 mmol) sulfur, 1.721 g (10 mmol) CuCl2·2H2O and 0.58 g (4.9 mmol) tin is loaded into a 100 mL Teflon-lined autoclave. Anhydrous ethylenediamine fills up to 90% of total volume. Seal; hold at 140–180°C for 15 h; cool naturally to room temperature; filter, wash several times with distilled water and absolute ethanol, and vacuum-dry at 60°C for 4 h.

The Experimental section states nominal purity greater than 99.9% for sulfur, CuCl2·2H2O and elemental tin; it does not state a purity for ethylenediamine. The workup says the precipitate was washed with distilled water and absolute ethanol "for several times"; no numeric wash count or solvent volumes are given.

items.title: XPS
paragraphs: XPS peak ratio Cu:Sn:S = 1.986:1:3.035; authors say EDX/chemical analysis agrees but provide no underlying values. No obvious chloride, elemental Sn or S impurity is reported above XPS resolution of 1 at%. Cu 2p peak FWHM are 1.9 and 2.4 eV; no Cu 2p3/2 satellite leads authors to infer Cu+ only. Sn 3d energies 486.8/495.2 eV are compared with SnS2; S 2p 161.9/162.8 eV are compared with chalcopyrite CuFeS2.

items.title: Absorption and conductivity
paragraphs: Aqueous nanocrystal solution: minor shoulder 530 nm (2.34 eV), which the source says “can be regarded as” an exciton peak, and edge ca. 660 nm (1.88 eV). Cited bulk (1362 nm, 0.91 eV) and film (700 nm, 1.77 eV) values are literature comparators, not this sample; authors attribute the blue shift to quantum-size effects. Four-probe conductivity on cold-pressed circular samples of 2R = 1.2 cm (source notation) from 18–300 K. Figure 5 is log σ versus 10³/T; no values are digitized.
The cuvette is silica, path length 1 cm; the main article does not state quartz.

reader_sections.title: Mechanism, controls and separate condition statements

items.title: Author-proposed mechanism
paragraphs: Authors discuss sulfur activation, a Cu–ethylenediamine complex and an Sn2S6^4−-type oligomer. These are interpretations, not isolated or measured intermediate species.

The authors mention tin or SnCl2 as raw-material contexts when discussing sulfur activation and contrast SnCl4; SnCl2 is not specified here as an executable recipe or assigned an independent outcome. Source locator: main PDF p. 3 (printed 172), mechanism discussion.

evidence.locator: main PDF p. 3 (printed 172), Results and discussion
main PDF p. 3 (printed 172), mechanism discussion of tin, SnCl2 and SnCl4

items.title: Separate control outcomes
paragraphs: Tin plus sulfur in ethylenediamine at 180°C for 12 h yielded an en/Sn/S coordination compound rather than unspecified binary tin sulfide (specific stoichiometry not identified). Replacing elemental tin with SnCl4 yielded Cu2SnS3. Benzene and ethanol solvent controls yielded mixtures of copper sulfide and tin sulfide, with no Cu2SnS3. Charge amounts and full conditions for the benzene/ethanol and SnCl4 controls are not reported; these are not variants of the main recipe.

evidence.locator: main PDF p. 3 (printed 172), Results and discussion

notes: Control outcomes are not added as product recipe conditions.

items.title: Keep temperature claims distinct
paragraphs: Authors call 140°C/15 h optimum. Lower temperature or shorter time gave incomplete reaction/decreased yield and crystallinity; below 100°C did not initiate. Separately, p. 4 reports grains up to 50 nm at 180°C/15 h. No characterization figure is assigned to that exact run.

source_gaps: SI not located/verified; absence not established.
No absolute solvent volume, reaction pressure, detailed ramp/cool, wash volumes and numerical wash-cycle count (the source only says "for several times"), yield or replicates.
No unit-cell values/CIF, EDX values, optical concentration or digitized conductivity values.
The 180°C/15 h upper grain-size outcome is a separate source-defined variant; its batch, phase characterization and Figure 1–5 assignment remain unknown.

The main Experimental section states nominal purity >99.9% only for sulfur, CuCl2·2H2O and elemental tin; no purity is stated for ethylenediamine (main PDF p. 1, printed p. 170). Washing is described as "for several times" (main PDF p. 2, printed p. 171), with no numeric cycle count or solvent volume.

The article names the solvent as anhydrous ethylenediamine; the C2H8N2 formula is a name-derived reference identity, not a formula printed in the main article. The authors use "en" as shorthand in discussion.
conflicts: General 140–180°C/15 h range, 140°C/15 h optimum and separate 180°C/15 h grain observation remain separate contexts.
Mechanistic species are proposed interpretations, not measured intermediates.
